---
title: "5. Reusable subcircuits"
subtitle: "Compose a two-stage filter without losing names"
julia:
  env: ["JULIA_PROJECT=../../.."]
---

```{julia}
#| include: false
using Pkg
Pkg.activate("../..")
using Amber
```

Hierarchy is useful once a circuit contains a repeated idea. A subcircuit has
explicit ports and parameters, then can be instantiated many times.

```{julia}
@subcircuit RCSection(input, output, reference; R=1kΩ, C=10nF) begin
    R1 = resistor(input, output; value=R)
    C1 = capacitor(output, reference; value=C)
    observe(voltage(output), current(R1))
end

@circuit TwoStageLowPass begin
    gnd = ground()
    input = node()
    middle = node()
    output = node()

    Source = voltage_source(input, gnd; ac=1V)
    First = RCSection(input, middle, gnd; R=1kΩ, C=10nF)
    Second = RCSection(middle, output, gnd; R=2kΩ, C=20nF)
    Load = resistor(output, gnd; value=100kΩ)

    observe(voltage(input), voltage(middle), voltage(output))
end
```

Assignments name the instances `First` and `Second`. Their internal elements
therefore have paths such as `First.R1` and `Second.C1`.

```{julia}
filter = TwoStageLowPass();
instances(filter)
devices(filter; under="First")
println(describe(filter))
```

Run the same analysis as for a flat circuit:

```{julia}
response = small_signal(filter, 10Hz => 1MHz; source=:Source, points=301);
first_stage = voltage(response, Symbol("First.output"))
final_output = voltage(response, :output)

(magnitude(first_stage[1]), magnitude(final_output[end]))
```

Port nets can be addressed using either their top-level name (`middle`) or a
qualified subcircuit port (`First.output`). Internal nets and devices require
their hierarchy-qualified path.

Hierarchy does not create a separate numerical simulator. Amber elaborates the
design into one compiled topology while retaining paths for results,
parameters, and diagnostics.
